envelope.description: Set the depth bound from the t3 measurement and pin it with two tests

body.title: Set the depth bound from the t3 measurement and pin it with two tests
body.summary: Choose the renderer's depth-bound value from what t3's narrow-pane measurement actually recorded, not an invented constant. The bound is a SAFETY limit against malformed or hostile structure — it must sit strictly above the MEASURED real maximum under a NAMED metric — element-nesting depth 4 across the four records, 7 levels of rendered DOM inside the slot — with stated headroom — and the value plus its reasoning go into the BUILD record. Alternative a4 was rejected precisely for making a bound a routine presentation rule that would fire on the majority of real records; this task exists to keep the line between guard and truncation feature on the right side. Gated on t3 because the LLD left this open deliberately: the right value depends on what nesting costs in a narrow pane, which the visual read is the first thing able to answer.
acceptanceChecks: The chosen value is strictly greater than 9 — retained, but now justified by MEASUREMENT rather than inherited: 9 is more than double the element-nesting maximum of 4 that the walk actually counts, and above the 7 rendered-DOM levels the slot produces. The headroom and its justification are stated in the BUILD record and CITE `S004/evidence/t3-depth-measurement.md`, naming the metric — not a number someone picked
EVERY one of the four real records renders UNTRUNCATED — the bound is proved never to fire on authored content, which is the distinction that rejected a4
A synthetic over-deep structure TRIPS the guard, rendering the ux-unknown degradation at the cut point naming depth as the reason, and the walk terminates
The bound is a single named constant with no second hard-coded copy anywhere in the source string
MUTATION: removing the bound makes the pathological-structure test hang or fail

tests.name: a structure beyond the bound stops at the cut point and marks it with a depth-named ux-unknown, and the walk terminates
all four real records render COMPLETELY at the chosen bound — the guard is proved never to fire on authored content
the bound exists as a single named constant with no second hard-coded copy in the source string
MUTATION: removing the bound makes the pathological-structure test hang or fail
